| gunicorn 26.2.0: the default `access_log_format` is `%(h)s %(l)s %(u)s %(t)s "%(r)s" %(s)s %(b)s "%(f)s" "%(a)s"`, and `r` is method, raw URI and protocol, so the query string, client address, Basic-auth user, referrer and user agent are all printed. `--access-logformat` replaces it. Atoms used: `m` method, `U` path without query, `s` status, `b` response length or `-`, `M` duration in ms, `%({header}o)s` a response header named in lowercase (so `X-Request-ID` is `{x-request-id}o`). | The Messages API is `POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`; `anthropic-version` (`2023-06-01`) and `content-type: application/json` are required, and the key goes in `Authorization: Bearer` or in `x-api-key`, which the overview calls the legacy fallback for `Authorization`, still supported (the adapter sends `x-api-key`); `"stream": true` returns server-sent events in the order `message_start`, then per content block `content_block_start` / `content_block_delta` / `content_block_stop`, then one or more `message_delta`, then a final `message_stop`, with `ping` events anywhere; a text delta is `delta.type == "text_delta"` carrying `text`; `message_start` carries the resolved `model` and `usage.input_tokens`; the `usage` on `message_delta` is cumulative, so the last one is the output token count; new event types may be added and code must handle unknown ones gracefully (versioning policy), which the adapter does by skipping them; `claude-opus-5` is a current Claude API model id | Verified | https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/overview, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/streaming, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview | 2026-09-19 |
| `stop_reason` is one of `end_turn`, `max_tokens` (the response reached the `max_tokens` limit and is truncated), `stop_sequence`, `tool_use`, `pause_turn`, `refusal` and `model_context_window_exceeded`; in a stream it is null on `message_start` and provided on `message_delta`, in no other event. The adapter carries it on `Completion.stop_reason`, so Ask can mark a `max_tokens` answer incomplete, and fails a stream that ends without one | Verified | https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/handling-stop-reasons | 2026-09-19 |
| Claude Opus 5 (with Claude Fable 5 and 5.1) has safety classifiers that can decline a request; a refusal is a normal HTTP 200, not an error, with `stop_reason: "refusal"` and a `stop_details` whose `explanation` text is not stable; it can arrive before any output or mid-stream after partial output, and in either case the partial output is to be treated as incomplete and discarded; a mid-stream refusal bills the input and the output already streamed. The adapter raises `LlmError` on it, so no refused answer becomes a `Completion` and a streaming caller discards what it holds; the beta server-side `fallbacks` parameter is not sent | Verified | https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/refusals-and-fallback | 2026-09-19 |
| Claude API errors: 400 `invalid_request_error`, 401 `authentication_error`, 402 `billing_error`, 403 `permission_error`, 404 `not_found_error`, 409 `conflict_error` (resolve the conflict, then retry), 413 `request_too_large`, 429 `rate_limit_error`, 500 `api_error`, 504 `timeout_error`, 529 `overloaded_error`; 408 is not in the table; the official SDKs retry connection errors, rate limits and 5xx with exponential backoff, twice by default, honouring `retry-after` when present; a failure after a streaming response has begun arrives as an SSE `error` event on an HTTP 200, not as a status; every error body is `{type, error: {type, message}, request_id}` and every response carries a `request-id` header. The Python SDK's own retry rule (`_should_retry`) retries 408, 409, 429 and every status from 500 up. The adapter retries 408, 409, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504, 529 and connection failures, and only before the answer's body starts | Verified | https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/main/src/anthropic/_base_client.py | 2026-09-19 |
| RFC 9110: a 408 means the server did not receive a complete request in the time it was prepared to wait, and a client with a request in transit MAY repeat it on a new connection (15.5.9), which is why the adapter retries 408; `Retry-After` is an HTTP-date or delay-seconds, a non-negative decimal integer (10.2.3), and the adapter honours only delay-seconds in ASCII digits | Verified | https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-15.5.9, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-10.2.3 | 2026-09-19 |
| Python 3.12 `urllib.request`: `Request.add_unredirected_header` adds a header that is not added to a redirected request; `HTTPRedirectHandler.redirect_request` returns the new request, or raises `HTTPError` when no other handler should handle the URL; `build_opener` puts its own `HTTPRedirectHandler` in front only when the handlers given contain no subclass of it; `urlopen`'s `timeout` is for blocking operations like the connection attempt, so `LLM_TIMEOUT_S` bounds each socket operation, not the call, and `LLM_DEADLINE_S` bounds the call. That the default handler copies the request's headers, key included, onto the GET it follows a 301, 302 or 303 with was read in the 3.12 source and is pinned by `tests_llm.py` against a server on 127.0.0.1 | Verified | https://docs.python.org/3.12/library/urllib.request.html | 2026-09-19 |

| acc-mcp-tools, MCP `tools/call` in revisions 2026-07-28 and 2025-11-25: params carry `name` and optional `arguments`; a result carries `content` (a `text` block among others) and optionally `structuredContent`, and `isError`. Two error paths: an unknown tool or a request that fails the CallToolRequest schema is a JSON-RPC protocol error, -32602 in the examples; an API failure, an input validation error (a date in the wrong format, a value out of range) or a business-logic error is a tool execution error, a result with `isError: true`, so the model can correct itself. ## Library baseline (D-118, ADR 0065, researched 2026-09-30)

One row per instrument of `backend/apps/library/baseline/`, grouped by tranche, naming the
pages each fact was read from. EUR-Lex answered this build with a challenge page, so EU
acts were read through the Publications Office (the metadata notice and the Official
Journal text served by `publications.europa.eu/resource/celex/<CELEX>`), which carries the
same act; each record still cites its EUR-Lex ELI page for a reader. Every EU instrument's
official English title, ELI, entry into force and in-force status was then cross-checked
against its notice by a script, independently of the research: all agree, and the three
apparent differences are explained (Directive (EU) 2015/849's `inForceTo` is the day after
the notice's last day of validity, by the baseline's own rule; Delegated Regulation (EU)
2016/522 carries the title Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/788 gave it; the DLT Pilot's
notice lists a stray 2021 date beside its entry into force on 2022-06-22). The twelve EU sanctions regulations whose title was later amended carry their current title, sourced to the consolidated text read (2026-10-01).

| Finansinspektionen's company register (`https://www.fi.se/sv/vara-register/foretagsregistret/`): any search can be downloaded as semicolon-separated UTF-8 text with a BOM by adding `format=csv` (`index?query=<org nr>&format=csv`); the header is `Namn;Org.nummer;LEI kod;Huvudverksamhet;Övriga verksamheter;Tillstånd 1;Tillstånd 2;…`, each licence cell reads `YYYY-MM-DD - <licence>, enligt <law>`, other businesses are comma-separated, a search by org number returns that one company, and an empty search stops at exactly 10,000 rows. A company's page (`details?id=…`, found through the HTML search) lists its branches under the heading "Filialer" with links to each branch's page, whose address ends with the country in Swedish ("Danmark", "Hongkong"); branch rows in the CSV carry no org number and no country. There is no documented API for the register. FI's open data page: "FI:s data är fritt tillgänglig utan avgift och får fritt bearbetas och vidareutnyttjas", with "Ange källa, FI och datum" (PUBLIC_REGISTERS.md, TEN-07, TEN-08) | Verified (fetched) | https://www.fi.se/sv/vara-register/foretagsregistret/index?query=SEB&format=csv; https://www.fi.se/sv/vara-register/foretagsregistret/details?id=1356 and the branch page `details?id=15110`; https://www.fi.se/sv/om-fi/om-webbplatsen/oppen-data/ | 2026-10-05 |

### Library baseline, gb-acts (researched 2026-11-14, D-145, ADR 0070)

One row per instrument of `backend/apps/library/baseline/gb-acts.json`, the United Kingdom's
Acts of Parliament. Each Act was read on legislation.gov.uk on 2026-11-14 in its latest
revised version, through the data form the site gives every page (`<page>/data.xml`): the
contents for the short title, the year and chapter and the day the Act was passed, the
commencement section, and every section a duty cites, whose page says whether it is in
force, prospective or repealed. An Act's `inForceFrom` is given only where its own
commencement section brings provisions into force on the day the Act was passed; where the
Act came into force by order or in stages it is left out and the row says so. A duty's
`effectiveFrom` is the day its section came into force as the note on the section's own
page gives it, or the commencement provision or order the entry names in `fieldSources`
(where it came in by stages, the day from which it was in force for every purpose), and is
left out where neither gives one. Three Acts carry no duty: what they ask of a firm is in
regulations made under them or in the text of the Acts they amend. Statutory instruments,
assimilated EU law, the FCA Handbook and the PRA Rulebook are left for later tranches; the
one statutory instrument read here is the commencement order S.I. 2001/3538, article 2,
for the day two sections of FSMA 2000 came into force.

### Library baseline, de-acts (researched 2026-11-14, D-145, ADR 0070)

One row per instrument of `backend/apps/library/baseline/de-acts.json`. Each act was read on Gesetze im
Internet on 2026-11-14: its full text page for the official title, the Vollzitat, the Stand and the
footnotes, its XML file (`<act>/xml.zip`) for the sections, and every cited section again on its own page,
whose text a script compared with the XML. `officialRef` is the Vollzitat up to its first gazette
reference, which stays the same across amendments; the last amending act is the Stand given in the row.
An implements note is given only where the page's footnote on EU law names a directive that is still in
force, or where the act's own § 1 or the enacting act's footnote in the Bundesgesetzblatt says what it
carries out; where the footnote names no directive or only older ones, the row says so. Entry into force
is read in the page's own footnote (for the BGB in Art 1 of its introductory act) and is never computed;
where no official page states it, the row says "not read" and the record carries no date.

### Library baseline, ch-acts (researched 2026-11-14, D-145, ADR 0070)

One row per instrument of `backend/apps/library/baseline/ch-acts.json`. Fedlex's pages hold no text without a
browser, so each act was read on 2026-11-14 through Fedlex's own interfaces: the SPARQL endpoint
(`https://fedlex.data.admin.ch/sparqlendpoint`, JOLux ontology) for the work by its SR number or title, its
ELI, its German title with the date and the consolidation applicable on the research day, and the file store
(`https://fedlex.data.admin.ch/filestore/...`) for that consolidation's German HTML and Akoma Ntoso XML. Only
the German text was read; the English translations, which have no legal force, were not opened. The official
title is the title and short title of the text's own header, `officialRef` the endpoint's and the XML's
German name with the date followed by the SR number of the header, and `eliUri` the work's ELI on
`www.fedlex.admin.ch` with `/de`, without a version date. Entry into force is the date the act's own final
article prints ("Datum des Inkrafttretens" or "Inkrafttreten", with the Federal Council decision in its
footnote) and is never computed; where single provisions took effect on another day the row says so, and
where the endpoint's `jolux:dateEntryInForce` is that other day the row gives both. Every duty was read in
the article it cites, in the whole article, and a script compared each cited article's HTML with the XML of
the same version, confirmed that every cited paragraph and letter exists and is not repealed, and fetched
each file again (200, byte for byte the file read). Switzerland is in neither the EU nor the EEA, so no
record carries an implements note. Left out, with the reason: the Obligationenrecht (SR 220) was not opened,
because the acts read refer to it only for rules that hold for every company (accounting, audit and the
retention of records under Art. 958f) and name no provision of it that binds banks specifically; a federal
act on distributed ledger technology is not an act of its own in the SR: the Bundesgesetz vom 25. September
2020 zur Anpassung des Bundesrechts an Entwicklungen der Technik verteilter elektronischer Register (AS 2021
33, https://fedlex.data.admin.ch/eli/oc/2021/33) is an amending act for which the endpoint lists no
consolidated work, and its rules are read here where it put them, in the BankG, FIDLEG, FinfraG and BEG
(footnotes "Eingefügt durch ... BG vom 25. Sept. 2020 ..."); a search of the endpoint's consolidated works
found none whose German title names crypto-based assets ("kryptobasierte") or artificial intelligence
("künstliche Intelligenz"); and Art. 30 TJPG is not yet applicable. No ordinance of the Federal Council, of
FINMA or of the National Bank is in this tranche.

### Library baseline, lv-acts (researched 2026-11-14, D-145, ADR 0070)

One row per instrument of `backend/apps/library/baseline/lv-acts.json`. Each act was read on Likumi.lv on
2026-11-14, in Latvian, on its own page (`https://likumi.lv/ta/id/<number>-<name>`): the act's passport
("Tiesību akta pase") for the official title, the issuer, the status, the publication in Latvijas Vēstnesis
and the entry into force; the page's list of versions for the consolidated version in force on the day and
any later one; the act's closing note on EU directives for the implements note; and every cited section at
its anchor (`#p<section>`). The consolidated text informs and the publication in Latvijas Vēstnesis binds;
no English translation was used. `officialRef` is the title with the publication the passport names, which
stays the same across amendments. Entry into force is the passport's date and, where the act has one, its
own closing provision; it is never computed. A duty carries an effective date only where the act itself
puts a provision into application on a stated later day. A script then fetched each page again at the
address the record gives and compared the passport, the version in force, each anchor and the paragraphs
and points each `refLabel` names with the text (20 pages answered 200, 136 duties matched).

### Library baseline, at-acts (researched 2026-11-14, D-145, ADR 0070)

One row per instrument of `backend/apps/library/baseline/at-acts.json`. The website of the
Rechtsinformationssystem des Bundes answers a program with a security check, so every act was read on
2026-11-14 through its open-data interface: the consolidated federal law as in force on that day
(`https://data.bka.gv.at/ris/api/v2.6/Bundesrecht?Applikation=BrKons&Gesetzesnummer=<n>&Fassung.FassungVom=2026-11-14`),
then each paragraph in its own document of the document store
(`https://ogd.ris.bka.gv.at/Dokumente/Bundesnormen/<NOR>/<NOR>.html`). The act's title document (§ 0) gives
the long title, the gazette reference of the original version (StF) and the list of amendments; the key
and `officialRef` rest on that reference and never on an amendment. Where one gazette number enacted more
than one statute (BGBl. I Nr. 107/2017: the Börsegesetz 2018 and the Wertpapieraufsichtsgesetz 2018; BGBl. I
Nr. 116/2015: the Gemeinsamer Meldestandard-Gesetz beside two other acts), the key carries the act's
abbreviation after the reference; each gazette's title and issue date were read through the interface's
gazette application (`Applikation=BgblAuth&Bgblnummer=<number>/<year>&Teil.SucheInTeil1=true`). Entry into
force is read in the act's own commencement paragraph; where that paragraph names no calendar day
(Sanktionengesetz 2024, ESAEG) it is the Inkrafttretensdatum the RIS states on the documents of the
original version, and the row says so. It is never computed. An implements note is given where the act's
own text says what it carries out, or else from the CELEX numbers the RIS title document lists, and the
row says which. The ELI is the `Eli` field the interface returns for the title document. A script fetched
every obligation's page again on 2026-11-14 and checked that it answers 200, is the paragraph the duty
cites, is the version in force on the research day and holds every Absatz cited.

| Claim | Status | Source | Checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| BWG: Bankwesengesetz (BWG), BGBl. Nr. 532/1993, "Bundesgesetz über das Bankwesen (Bankwesengesetz – BWG)", entered into force 1994-01-01 (§ 107 Abs. 1: "Dieses Bundesgesetz tritt, soweit im folgenden nicht anderes bestimmt ist, mit dem 1. ### Library baseline, ee-acts (researched 2026-11-14, D-145, ADR 0070)

One row per instrument of `backend/apps/library/baseline/ee-acts.json`. Each act was read on Riigi Teataja on
2026-11-14 through the interface its own pages call, because the pages hold no text without a browser:
`/public-api/api/v1/akt/lyhendid` (the gazette's list of act abbreviations) gave each act's text id,
`/akt/<id>` its metadata with `kehtivId`, the version in force, and `/akt/<id>/txt` the Estonian text of that
version, whose header gives the publication reference of the version, the day it entered into force and the
act's original publication reference. The key and `officialRef` rest on that original reference, never on a
consolidated version's. Every duty was read in Estonian in the version in force on 2026-11-14; the English
translations, which Riigi Teataja calls unofficial, were not used. Entry into force is read in the act's own
section where it has one and otherwise in the text's header, and is never computed. An implements note names
the EU acts of the act's own footnote (for the IKS and the KrüTS, of its § 1); where the plain text leaves the
footnote out it was read in `/akt/<id>/xml`, and the row says so. The Eesti Panga seadus (RT I 1993, 28, 498,
text id 130062026013) was read too and is not in the tranche: it gives Eesti Pank powers and lays no duty on
a bank in its own words.

### Library baseline, nl-acts (researched 2026-11-14, D-145, ADR 0070)

One row per instrument of `backend/apps/library/baseline/nl-acts.json`. wetten.overheid.nl refused the
command-line read on 2026-11-14 (the connection was closed without an answer on every address, the site's
robots file included), so each act was read where Overheid.nl publishes the same consolidated law for
programs: the act's manifest in the official repository
(`repository.officiele-overheidspublicaties.nl/bwb/<BWB id>/manifest.xml`), which names every version, and
the XML file of the version in force on 2026-11-14; the BWB ids were found with the site's SRU search service
(`zoekservice.overheid.nl/sru/Search?x-connection=BWB`). The official title is the act's `intitule`, the
short title its `citeertitel`, and `officialRef` is the citation title with the Staatsblad reference of first
publication, all as the file prints them. Entry into force is the date the file's source data give for the
title (`inwerkingtreding`, with the Staatsblad that set it) and is never computed; for six acts the royal
decree itself was read in the Staatsblad (`zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl/stb-<year>-<number>.html`) and is
the record's source for the date; where a date is the start of a part only, the row says so. A duty carries
an effective date only where the file marks its article as newly inserted on a day after the act's start and
unchanged since; for an article amended later the file gives the day of the last amendment, which is not the
day the duty began, and the duty carries no date. A record's source link is the XML file of the version read, and each
duty's source label ends with the article's own Juriconnect address, as the file gives it, which is the
article's page on wetten.overheid.nl. An implements note is given only where the act's title, preamble,
a heading or its first article says what it carries out. The Dutch acts that carry out DORA, MiCA and the
Transfer of Funds Regulation (BWBR0049942, BWBR0050660, BWBR0050680) are amending acts whose rules sit in
the Wft and the Wwft; no act carrying out the AI Act was found in the BWB on 2026-11-14. Read and left out: the
Pensioenwet (BWBR0020809), whose duties bind pension providers and reach a bank or asset manager only through
the provider's own outsourcing duty in art. 34; the Wet toezicht financiële verslaggeving (BWBR0020369),
which holds the AFM's powers over issuers' financial reporting; the Wet inzake spaarbewijzen (BWBR0003797),
whose rules apply only while a scheme is declared generally binding; and the Noodwet financieel verkeer
(BWBR0003173), whose articles 3 to 32 are not in force until a royal decree brings them into force in
extraordinary circumstances (art. 2).

### Library baseline, gb-si (researched 2026-11-14, D-145, ADR 0070)

One row per instrument of `backend/apps/library/baseline/gb-si.json`, the United Kingdom's
statutory instruments. Each was read on legislation.gov.uk on 2026-11-14 through the data form
the site gives every page (`<page>/data.xml`): the contents for the title, the number, the date of
the latest revised version and the changes the site lists as not yet applied; the introduction
for the opening words, which name the maker and the empowering provisions; the whole revised
text, to find the duties; and every provision a duty cites, again on its own page. The issuer is
the maker those words name: "The Treasury" is `hm-treasury`, "The Secretary of State" is
`hm-government`; none of these instruments was made by the Commissioners for HMRC. `inForceFrom`
is the day the instrument's own commencement provision, or the editorial note on it, gives for its
first provisions; a duty's `effectiveFrom` is the later day its provision applies from, read on the
provision's own page, in its commencement provision or on the page `fieldSources` names, and is
left out where none states it. No instrument carries an implements note: those made under the
European Communities Act 1972 name the directive only in their explanatory note, which says it is
not part of the instrument. The FCA Handbook and the PRA Rulebook were not opened, and retained EU
law held under `/eur/` is not in this tranche.

### Library baseline, de-verordnungen (researched 2026-11-14, D-145, ADR 0070)

One row per instrument of `backend/apps/library/baseline/de-verordnungen.json`, the regulations
(Rechtsverordnungen) made under the statutes of `de-acts`. Each regulation was found in the index of all
acts on Gesetze im Internet (`gii-toc.xml`) and read there on 2026-11-14: its full text page for the official
title, the Vollzitat, the Stand and the footnotes, its Eingangsformel for the issuer and the empowering
provision, its XML file (`<slug>/xml.zip`) for the sections, and every section a duty cites again on its own
page, whose text a script compared with the XML (143 pages, each 200). The issuer is the body the
regulation's own opening words name ("verordnet das Bundesministerium der Finanzen", "verordnet die
Bundesanstalt für Finanzdienstleistungsaufsicht", "Es verordnen ... die Bundesregierung"); where the page prints no
Eingangsformel, the footnote to the title that names the maker was read instead, and the row says so.
`officialRef` is the Vollzitat up to its first gazette reference; the last amending act is the Stand given in
the row. Entry into force is read in the regulation's own entry-into-force section, in the footnote to the
title or, for the AWV, in the Stand line, and is never computed: where the section says only "am Tag nach
der Verkündung", the row says "not read" and the record carries no date. An implements note is given only
where the official note on EU law or the regulation's own text names an EU act.

### Library baseline, nl-besluiten (researched 2026-11-14, D-145, ADR 0070)

One row per instrument of `backend/apps/library/baseline/nl-besluiten.json`, the decrees and regulations made under the
statutes of `nl-acts`. wetten.overheid.nl closed every command-line read on 2026-11-14, as it did for the statutes, and
was not read; each regulation was found with the publisher's SRU search service
(`zoekservice.overheid.nl/sru/Search?x-connection=BWB`, filtered on `overheidbwb.geldigheidsdatum=2026-11-14`) and read
where Overheid.nl publishes the same consolidated law for programs: its manifest in the official repository
(`repository.officiele-overheidspublicaties.nl/bwb/<BWB id>/manifest.xml`), which names every version, and the XML
file of the version in force on 2026-11-14. The official title is the file's `intitule`, the short title its
`citeertitel` or the abbreviation the BWB's own data give, and `officialRef` the citation title with the Staatsblad
or Staatscourant reference of first publication as the file prints it. The issuer is the maker the text names in its
title, opening words or closing, read on the page; where the page names none or names two makers the row says so
and the BWB's own data (`soort-regeling`, the responsible body) decide, as the prompt's authority rule allows. A
royal decree (algemene maatregel van bestuur) is filed under `regering-nl`, a regulation of the Minister of Finance
under `ministerie-van-financien`, and a regulation of De Nederlandsche Bank or the Autoriteit Financiële Markten
under `dnb` or `afm`. Entry into force is read in the regulation's own entry-into-force article where it names a day,
in the royal decree in the Staatsblad (`zoek.officielebekendmakingen.nl/stb-<year>-<number>.html`) where the
regulation ties its start to a statute or decree that decree brings into force on a named day, and otherwise in the
file's source data for the title; it is never computed from an issue date. A duty carries an effective date only
where the file marks its article as newly inserted after the instrument's start and unchanged since. Each record's
source link is the XML file of the version read, and each duty's source label ends with the article's Juriconnect
address, which is its page on wetten.overheid.nl. Found and left out, by issuer: the sanctions regulations under
the Sanctiewet 1977 (among them the Sanctieregeling terrorisme 2002, BWBR0013736, Stcrt. 2002, 104, and the
Sanctieregeling territoriale integriteit Oekraïne 2014, BWBR0034955, Stcrt. 2014, 8792), whose maker is the Minister
of Foreign Affairs 'handelende in overeenstemming met de Minister van Financiën', not a seeded authority; De
Nederlandsche Bank's 'Beleidsregel Individueel Klantbeeld Wft 2017' (BWBR0039826) and 'Beleidsregel Reikwijdte en
Uitvoering Depositogarantiestelsel' (BWBR0039820), which are policy rules, not regulations; and the Besluit
beheerst beloningsbeleid Wft (BWBR0029072), an amending decree whose rules sit in the decrees it amended. The
Regeling liquiditeit Wft (BWBR0020673) and the Regeling liquiditeit Wft 2011 (BWBR0028903) are no longer in force
(the BWB gives them end dates of 2011-04-30 and 2015-12-31); only the credit unions' liquidity regulation remains.

### Library baseline, ch-verordnungen (researched 2026-11-14, D-145, ADR 0070)

One row per instrument of `backend/apps/library/baseline/ch-verordnungen.json`, Switzerland's federal ordinances
(Verordnungen) that a bank answers to. Fedlex's pages hold no text without a browser, so each ordinance was read on
2026-11-14 through Fedlex's own interfaces, as for `ch-acts`: the SPARQL endpoint
(`https://fedlex.data.admin.ch/sparqlendpoint`, JOLux ontology) for the work by its SR number or German title, its
ELI, its German title with the date and the consolidation applicable on the research day, and the file store
(`https://fedlex.data.admin.ch/filestore/...`) for that consolidation's German HTML and Akoma Ntoso XML. Only the
German text was read; no English translation was opened. The issuer is the body the ordinance's own preamble names
as its maker ("Der Schweizerische Bundesrat, gestützt auf ... verordnet:", "Die Eidgenössische Finanzmarktaufsicht
(FINMA), gestützt auf ...", "Die Schweizerische Nationalbank (SNB), gestützt auf ..."), and a script confirmed each
preamble's opening words; the empowering statute and articles named in each row and `sourceLabel` are read in the same
preamble. The official title is the title and short title of the text's own header, `officialRef` the endpoint's and
the XML's German name with the date followed by the SR number of the header (three rows say where that came to more
than the 200 characters the record takes), and `eliUri` the work's ELI on `www.fedlex.admin.ch` with `/de`. Entry
into force is the day the ordinance's own final article prints ("Diese Verordnung tritt am ... in Kraft"), checked by
script against that article, and is never computed; where a later consolidation is already published, the row says
so and the version in force on 2026-11-14 was read. Every duty was read in the whole article it cites; a script
compared each cited article's HTML with the XML of the same version, confirmed that every cited paragraph exists and
is not repealed, and fetched every file again (200, byte for byte the file read). Switzerland is in neither the EU
nor the EEA, so no record carries an implements note. Sanctions ordinances under the Embargo Act sit under
`regime:aml`; their issuer is the Federal Council. Read and left out, with the reason: the Insolvenzverordnung FINMA
(InsV-FINMA, SR 952.05, in force 1 October 2025), which by its Art. 48 repealed the Bankeninsolvenzverordnung-FINMA,
holds procedure for FINMA, liquidators and creditors and no duty a bank registers for its own business; the
Liquiditätsverordnung-FINMA (LiqV-FINMA, eli/cc/2026/383) and the Risikoverteilungsverordnung-FINMA (RVV-FINMA,
eli/cc/2026/247) enter into force on 1 January 2027 and are not in force on the research day; the Verordnung über
die Transparenz juristischer Personen (TJPV, SR 955.31), the Myanmar and Hamas sanctions ordinances (SR 946.231.157.5,
SR 946.231.09) and FINMA's ordinances on market risks, credit risks and the trading and banking book
(MarV-FINMA, KreV-FINMA, HBEV-FINMA) are binding and in force but were not written in this tranche. Ordinances whose
issuer is not a seeded authority were left out: the EJPD's ordinance on the maximum interest rate for consumer credit
(SR 221.214.111), fedpol's ordinance on the data standard of the reporting office's information system (VDIGw,
eli/cc/2026/440), the BAZG's anti-money laundering ordinance for bank precious metals trading (GwV-BAZG,
eli/cc/2022/597) and the Takeover Board's ordinance on public takeover offers (UEV, SR 954.195.1).

### Library baseline, at-verordnungen (researched 2026-11-14, D-145, ADR 0070)

One row per instrument of `backend/apps/library/baseline/at-verordnungen.json`, the regulations made under
Austria's statutes. The website of the Rechtsinformationssystem des Bundes answers a program with a security
check, so every regulation was read on 2026-11-14 through its open-data interface: the regulations in force on
that day were listed by index (`Applikation=BrKons&Index=37/02&Typ=V`, and the neighbouring indexes 21/05,
37/01, 37/03, 37/05, 20/06 and 12/05) and by full-text search for the empowering statutes, then each one was read
as consolidated on that day (`Applikation=BrKons&Gesetzesnummer=<n>&Fassung.FassungVom=2026-11-14`), paragraph by
paragraph in its own document of the document store (`https://ogd.ris.bka.gv.at/Dokumente/Bundesnormen/<NOR>/<NOR>.html`).
The title document (§ 0) gives the long title, the gazette reference of the original version (StF), the preamble
and the list of amendments. The issuer is the body the long title names as the regulation's maker, and it was
read again in the gazette's own title of the first publication (`Applikation=BgblAuth&Bgblnummer=<number>/<year>`),
which also showed that no gazette number in the tranche holds a second regulation, so no key carries a suffix.
The key and `officialRef` rest on the StF reference; the empowering provision in each `sourceLabel` is the one the
preamble names. Entry into force is read in the regulation's own commencement paragraph; where that paragraph names
no calendar day or the regulation has none, it is the Inkrafttretensdatum the RIS states on the title document of
the original version, and the row says so. It is never computed. An implements note is given only where the
regulation's text or its title document names an EU act. A script fetched every page again on 2026-11-14 and
checked that it answers 200, is the paragraph the duty cites, is in force on the research day by the interface's
index and holds every Absatz cited. The regulations found and left out, and the supervisor's circulars, are listed
in the tranche's report, not here.

### Library baseline, lv-noteikumi (researched 2026-11-14, D-145, ADR 0070)

One row per instrument of `backend/apps/library/baseline/lv-noteikumi.json`: ten regulations of the
Cabinet of Ministers (Ministru kabinets, level `government_regulation`) and seventeen of Latvijas Banka
(level `authority_regulation`). They were found on Likumi.lv on 2026-11-14 through each statute's own list
of the acts issued under it ("Uz tiesību akta pamata izdotie", the list the page's "Saistītie dokumenti"
tab loads from `https://likumi.lv/ajax/saistitie.php?do=show&doc_id=<statute>&type=rev-933`), read for all
twenty statutes of `lv-acts`; each list gives every act's issuer, kind, number and status, and
only acts marked "spēkā esošs" were taken. Each regulation was then read in Latvian on its own page
(`https://likumi.lv/ta/id/<number>-<name>`): the passport ("Tiesību akta pase") for the official title, the
issuer ("Izdevējs"), the number, the adoption date, the status, the publication in Latvijas Vēstnesis, the
entry into force and any loss of force; the opening lines of the text for the maker ("Ministru kabineta
noteikumi Nr. …", "Latvijas Bankas noteikumi Nr. …") and the preamble ("Izdoti saskaņā ar …") naming the
empowering statute and section, which each entry's `sourceLabel` gives in English; the page's list of
versions for the consolidated version in force on the day and any later one; the closing note on EU law for
the implements note; and every cited point at its anchor (`#p<point>`). The consolidated text informs and
the publication in Latvijas Vēstnesis binds; no English translation was used. `officialRef` is the
regulation's citation as Latvian law writes it, the maker, the adoption date and the number, followed by the
publication the passport names (a Cabinet regulation's number restarts every year, so the date is part of
the citation); the long official titles do not fit the field's 200 characters. Entry into force is the
passport's date and, where the regulation has one, its own closing point; it is never computed. An
implements note is given only where the closing note names a directive; where it names only EBA or ESMA
guidelines, none is given. A script then fetched each page again at the address the record gives and
compared the passport, the version in force, the opening lines, each anchor and every point and sub-point
each `refLabel` names with the text (27 pages answered 200, 131 duties matched). Regulations of the former
Finanšu un kapitāla tirgus komisija are all marked "zaudējis spēku" in those lists (310 of them); each
Latvijas Banka regulation here that replaced one says so in its closing points, and the row names it.

### Library baseline, ee-maarused (researched 2026-11-14, D-145, ADR 0070)

One row per instrument of `backend/apps/library/baseline/ee-maarused.json`. Each regulation was found and read on
Riigi Teataja on 2026-11-14 through the interface its own pages call, because the pages hold no text without a
browser. The site's own script (`main-O6LZF5XV.js` and `chunk-D25hlgc3.js`, fetched from the site) calls
`/public-api/api/v1/akt/<id>/rakendus-aktid` for an act's implementing acts; asked for each statute of `ee-acts`
by the id of its version in force, the interface answered with the regulations issued under it, each with its
issuer, number and validity (for the Finantskriisi ennetamise ja lahendamise seadus, the Isikuandmete kaitse
seadus and the Krüptovaraturu seadus it answered that the act has none). Each regulation was then read as the
statutes were: `/akt/<id>` for its metadata with `kehtivId`, the version in force, and `/akt/<id>/txt` for the
Estonian text of that version, whose header names the issuer ("Väljaandja"), the version's publication reference
and the day it entered into force, and, for a consolidated text, the regulation's original publication reference
and entry into force. The key and `officialRef` rest on that original reference; a regulation first published in
the Riigi Teataja Lisa (RTL) takes `ee-rtl-`. Where the text is the original text ("algtekst-terviktekst") and the
regulation has no entry-into-force section, its entry into force is the day its header gives for that first and
only version. Every duty was read in Estonian in the version in force on 2026-11-14. No regulation chosen carries
a footnote on EU law (the XML of each was searched); an implements note is given only where the regulation's own
text names the EU act it serves, and the row quotes where.

### Library baseline, lv-noteikumi-2 (researched 2026-11-14, D-145, ADR 0070)

One row per instrument of `backend/apps/library/baseline/lv-noteikumi-2.json`: six regulations of the
Cabinet of Ministers (Ministru kabinets, level `government_regulation`) and twenty-three of Latvijas Banka
(level `authority_regulation`), the further regulations the `lv-noteikumi` researcher listed as found and
not written. Each was found again on Likumi.lv on 2026-11-14 in the list of acts issued under its statute
("Uz tiesību akta pamata izdotie", loaded from
`https://likumi.lv/ajax/saistitie.php?do=show&doc_id=<statute>&type=rev-933`), read for the Credit
Institutions Law, the Law on Payment Services and Electronic Money, the anti-money-laundering law, the
Financial Instrument Market Law, the Investment Firms Law, the Covered Bonds Law, the Deposit Guarantee
Law, the Crypto-Asset Services Law and the Law on Taxes and Fees; only acts marked "spēkā esošs" were
taken, and none was already in the baseline under its key or its citation. Each regulation was read in
Latvian on its own page (`https://likumi.lv/ta/id/<number>-<name>`) as the `lv-noteikumi` section
describes: the passport for the title, issuer, number, adoption date, status, publication, entry into
force and any loss of force; the opening lines for the maker and the preamble ("Izdoti saskaņā ar …"),
which each entry's `sourceLabel` gives in English and each row quotes as printed; the list of versions for
the version in force on the day; the closing note on EU law for the implements note; and every cited point
at its anchor (`#p<point>`). The consolidated text informs and the publication in Latvijas Vēstnesis binds;
no English translation was used. `officialRef`, entry into force and the implements note follow the
`lv-noteikumi` rules. A script then fetched each page again at the address the record gives and compared
the passport, the version in force, the opening lines, the preamble, the entry-into-force point, the
directives the closing note names, each anchor and every point and sub-point each `refLabel` names with the
text (29 pages answered 200, 119 duties matched). Where a duty of `lv-acts` or `lv-noteikumi` already holds
the statutory duty a regulation fills in, the row says so and the duties here register only what the
regulation adds. Of the listed regulations, these were read and left out: Latvijas Banka's No 241 on
acquiring qualifying holdings (it binds the proposed acquirer, whoever that is, not the institution) and
No 337 on reporting breaches to Latvijas Banka (it binds the reporting person and Latvijas Banka), and the
Cabinet's No 396 of 2022 on the shared customer due diligence tool (it binds the tool's provider and the
Data State Inspectorate). Latvijas Banka's No 366 on the anti-money-laundering methodology of a credit
institution in insolvency or liquidation, met in the same list, binds its administrator and was left out.

### Library baseline, ch-verordnungen-2 (researched 2026-11-14, D-145, ADR 0070)

One row per instrument of `backend/apps/library/baseline/ch-verordnungen-2.json`, the third Swiss tranche: the further
federal ordinances that the `ch-verordnungen` researcher found binding and did not write, and further sanctions ordinances of
the same kind met on the way. Each ordinance was read on 2026-11-14 exactly as for `ch-verordnungen`: Fedlex's SPARQL
endpoint (`https://fedlex.data.admin.ch/sparqlendpoint`, JOLux ontology) for the work by its SR number or German title, its
ELI, its German title and the consolidation applicable on the research day, and the file store
(`https://fedlex.data.admin.ch/filestore/...`) for that consolidation's German HTML and Akoma Ntoso XML. Only the German
text was read; no English translation was opened. The issuer is the body the ordinance's own preamble names as its maker
("Der Schweizerische Bundesrat, gestützt auf ... verordnet:", "Die Eidgenössische Finanzmarktaufsicht (FINMA), gestützt auf
..."), confirmed by script, and the empowering basis in each row and `sourceLabel` is read in the same preamble. The
official title is the title and short title of the text's own header, `officialRef` the endpoint's and the XML's German
name with the date followed by the SR number of the header (two rows say where that differs), and `eliUri` the work's ELI
on `www.fedlex.admin.ch` with `/de`. Entry into force is the day the ordinance's own final article prints, checked by
script against that article and never computed. Every duty was read in the whole article it cites; a script compared each
cited article's HTML with the XML of the same version, confirmed that every cited paragraph exists and is not repealed, and
fetched every file again (200, byte for byte the file read). No record carries an implements note. Sanctions ordinances
under the Embargo Act and the asset freeze ordinances under the SRVG sit under `regime:aml`; their issuer is the Federal
Council; the names of listed persons and entities are not reproduced. Every candidate was searched for in all
`backend/apps/library/baseline/*.json` by key and by official reference first; none was there. Read and left out, with the
reason: the FATCA-Verordnung (SR 672.933.60, eli/cc/2014/315), which the endpoint records as no longer in force (status
"Nicht mehr in Kraft", end of applicability 2015-03-31, its one consolidation dated 2014-06-30 and published as PDF only);
the SRVG ordinances on Tunisia (SR 196.127.58) and Ukraine (SR 196.127.67), whose Art. 4 last extended them to 18 January
2021 and 27 February 2023 and which the endpoint records as no longer in force; the Aufsichtsprüfverordnung FINMA (SR
956.161.1, eli/cc/2024/643), which by its Art. 1 governs how audit firms audit and binds no supervised firm; the Verordnung
zum Finanzmarktaufsichtsgesetz (SR 956.11), which governs FINMA's international and regulatory work and binds no firm; and
the Lebanon ordinance (SR 946.231.148.9), an arms embargo with no freeze, no ban on making funds available and no duty to
report, whose one duty reaching a bank (no financing linked to arms for Lebanon, Art. 1 Abs. 2) is below the tranche's floor
of two duties. Found binding and in force and not written in this tranche: the sanctions ordinances on Guinea (SR
946.231.138.1), Guinea-Bissau (SR 946.231.138.3) and the persons connected with the attack in Beirut (SR 946.231.10).
